mode achieved: static review of the final tree (snapshot task12-final). Read in full all 19 screen 24 test and helper files, the 8 new or helper design-system test files (testID, Row, PendingAction, PressableLink, tokens.test, tokens.test.helper, status.test.helper, Select.test.helper), Glyph.test.native.tsx:1-40, the shared helpers (spy, route, viewport, widths, window setup), src/shell/useApi.ts and its test, the real overview route, the restated-literal rule and its config, CONTRIBUTING.md, Tasks 6b to 12 and the traceability section of the cleanup plan, and the ledger lines of Tasks 6b, 9 and 9b. Compared all 64 in-scope test files of the two trees (lines and expect counts). Ran 3 probes from the lane (each file checked with cmp against the snapshot): ESLint on a scratch screen test (10 restatement forms), check-language on two scratch tests, and check-language on src/design-system plus src/screens of the snapshot. Ran 0 tests (NOT RUN: the brief forbids Jest and Stryker; a proof command is given where a claim needs a run).
verdict: 7 of 8 round-1 keys closed and 1 partly closed (shared token values, two screen assertions left). One regression: the health and freshness mark tables are now in-sample oracles. New: the restated-literal rule misses composed copy, plus two nits.

## Regressions

🟡 major  The Health card and freshness tests read their expected marks from the table they test, so a swapped level or tone passes everything
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/HealthCard.test.native.tsx#marks-read-from-table-under-test
- where: HealthCard.test.native.tsx:31 and :39-45: markOf builds the expected glyph and tone from `levelMarks[level]`, used at :73, :90 and :106; :94-97 checks only that the glyph names are unique. HeaderRow.test.native.tsx:30 and :83-88 read `freshnessMarks[tone]` in the same way; :92-95 checks uniqueness only. The blocks read the same objects (HealthCard.tsx:15, HeaderRow.tsx:13) from HealthCard.styles.ts:11-16 and HeaderRow.styles.ts:25-30. Round 1's typed tables, LEVELS in the repo's HealthCard.test.native.tsx and FRESHNESS in its HeaderRow.test.native.tsx, were deleted. They were the only independent holders (green ● good, amber ▲ waiting, red ■ critical, unknown ? muted; and per freshness its glyph, size, mark tone and text tone).
- why: the expected value is read at assertion time from the same object the block draws from. Any edit to the table, such as swapping the red and green glyphs, giving red the tone 'good', drawing stale as a dot, or making the stale text muted, moves the expectation with it. This is an in-sample oracle for a BR-39 rule: the shape tells the levels apart without colour. My round-1 fix said to delete "glyph character, size and color tables" together with the design-system looks. The character and pixel look belong to Glyph.test.native.tsx:9-40. Which level gets which glyph and tone is the screen's own decision, and it needed to stay typed.
- fix: type the screen's decision once in each block test and use it as the oracle. In HealthCard.test.native.tsx: `const MARKS = { green: { glyph: 'ragGreen', tone: 'good' }, amber: { glyph: 'ragAmber', tone: 'waiting' }, red: { glyph: 'ragRed', tone: 'critical' }, unknown: { glyph: 'ragUnknown', tone: 'muted' } } as const`; markOf reads MARKS instead of levelMarks, and one more assertion pins the key set: `expect(Object.keys(levelMarks)).toEqual(Object.keys(MARKS))`. Do the same in HeaderRow.test.native.tsx for the glyph, size, tone and text of the four freshness tones, with values from the rag and freshness rules of wireframes/assets/wireframe.css. Each value is a single camelCase word, which the restated-literal rule allows (eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js:31-34). Then plant the swap below and expect red.
- approach-changing: no, two typed tables in two test files
- trigger: swap the glyphs at HealthCard.styles.ts:12 and :14 (green: 'ragRed', red: 'ragGreen'). Meridian's computed line, 'Off track' (model.test.ts:165), then draws the green dot next to its words. HealthCard.test.native.tsx:73, :90 and :106 build the expectation from the edited table and pass, and :94-97 still counts four distinct names. Swapping fresh and stale at HeaderRow.styles.ts:26-27 makes a stale snapshot show the fresh dot, and HeaderRow.test.native.tsx:83-88 still passes. NOT RUN (the brief forbids Jest). Proof command after the edit: cd apps/metis && rtk proxy pnpm exec jest src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks; expect 0 failures.
- guard-bypass: the oracle is the table under test. Stryker never mutates it: stryker.config.json:14 excludes src/**/*.styles.ts, and Stryker has no member-swap mutator anyway. e2e reads only the freshness words (e2e/web/states.spec.ts:25, :48 and :55; e2e/web/brand.spec.ts:48-51), and no spec reads a mark. Glyph.test.native.tsx:9-40 pins the character of each glyph name, not which level uses it.

## New findings

🟡 major  The restated-literal rule only matches whole literals, so the composed sentences that made up most of round 1's restated copy pass lint
- key: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js#whole-literal-match-only
- where: CONTRIBUTING.md:57-60 and :71-72; eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js:95 (`table.get(value)` compares the whole string), :110 (a template literal with an expression is skipped) and :31-34 (isDistinctive drops numbers and strings under four characters). It applies to every non-model test of src/screens and src/shell.
- why: most of round 1's restated copy was composed: the health warning sentence typed 4 times, the empty-upcoming sentence 5 times, the more rows. The model composes these sentences from templates, so no dictionary holds them as a value and the rule cannot see them. No non-model screen test types one today, because Task 9 removed them by hand. Nothing stops plan C's screens from bringing them back, and the written rule (typed sentences only in model tests, CONTRIBUTING.md:71-72) has no gate.
- probe: ESLint from the lane, on a scratch file linted through stdin as src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/Probe.test.native.tsx: 3 errors on 10 lines. Reported: 'Not built yet', `Nothing is overdue.` and 'Meridian CGI Campaign'. Not reported: 'Not built ' + 'yet', the composed empty-upcoming sentence, the composed health warning, '+ 5 more · open in Focus', '3 of 12 work items done', '9' and /Nothing is overdue/. Scratch file: review2-test-design-screens/probe-lint/Probe.test.native.tsx in the scratchpad.
- fix: in no-restated-literals.js, three changes. (1) Turn each dictionary template into a pattern: escape the static text and replace each {slot} with .+?. Then report a non-model test literal that matches a template whose static text holds at least two words. (2) Report a literal that contains a protected multi-word value as a substring. (3) Fold a + concatenation of literals into one string before the check. Add the probe's six missed string lines as invalid cases in eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.test.js. A bare number stays allowed, since a '9' that matches is chance.
- approach-changing: no, a rule extension with its tests
- trigger: a plan C block test types `expect(screen.getByText('Declared health is better than computed. Delivery: 9 overdue items including 3 milestones. Risk: 1 critical risk without mitigation.')).toBeOnTheScreen()`, the WARNING constant of round 1's HealthCard.test.native.tsx:12-13. gate:lint passes. The next rewording of the health templates in strings/en.ts then breaks that file and every copy of it, which is the round-1 multiplier.
- guard-bypass: the rule compares whole literals with dictionary values (:95), and a composed sentence is never a value of en.ts. The model-test exemption (:97) marks where sentences may live, but nothing reports them anywhere else.

💭 nit  Three screen test helpers re-implement a shared one beside it
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.test.helper.tsx#helpers-beside-shared-ones
- where: Screen.test.helper.tsx:15 types the overview API path that src/mocks/handlers.ts:81 serves (src/core/api/client.test.ts:11 types it a third time; that file is part A's). Screen.links.test.native.tsx:23 defines a second `pathOf(route)`, meaning the href without its query, beside the shared `pathOf(pathname, params)` of src/route.test.helper.ts:7 that CONTRIBUTING.md:89-90 names. Screen.states.test.native.tsx:80-91 hand-rolls the held answer that `hold` (Screen.test.helper.tsx:50-62) already provides, only to count calls.
- why: maintenance only, and a drift fails loudly: a renamed endpoint makes every override in the Screen tests miss, and mockServer then fails the test (CONTRIBUTING.md:95). The two functions named pathOf, with two meanings, mislead whoever copies these files next.
- fix: export the path from handlers.ts (for example `export const OVERVIEW_PATH = \`${BASE}/projects/:projectId/overview\``) and build OVERVIEW from it. Rename the local helper to `pathnameOf`. Give hold an optional start (`hold(server, answer, { from: 2 })`) and use it in the retry test.
- approach-changing: no, mechanical

💭 nit  CONTRIBUTING bans tree walks in every test, but the design-system tests walk their own components
- key: CONTRIBUTING.md#tree-walk-rule-scope
- where: CONTRIBUTING.md:84-87 ("Do not re-assert a design-system style in a screen test or walk the element tree (.parent, .children, child indexes)"). Design-system tests walk their own component's tree in at least 40 lines across 11 files (grep for .parent, .children and screen.root, cut at 40 hits), for example Card.test.native.tsx:41-42 and :54-55, ListRow.test.native.tsx:77-80 and :145-148, BarTrack.test.native.tsx:24-38, StatePanel.test.native.tsx:73-89, Meter.test.native.tsx:20-35 and Select.test.android.tsx:120-134.
- why: the sentence reads as a ban for every test. The next reviewer either flags 40 legitimate lines or learns that the rule is optional. A component's own test walking its tree is defensible, because the structure is what it proves, but adding one wrapper View to such a component now breaks those lines.
- fix: scope the sentence: "In a screen or shell test, do not re-assert a design-system style or walk the element tree; a design-system test may walk its own component's tree." Or give those parts testIDs, as testID.test.native.tsx:22 already does for the outer element.
- approach-changing: no, one sentence
